  DATE: January 31, 2023

  TO:  The Honorable Mayor and City Council
  FROM:  Ron Bow, City Manager
  SUBJECT:  Adopt a Resolution extending a local emergency resulting from the Mass
  Murder on January 21, 2023 and authorizing the City Manager to issue
  an Executive Order to direct the California Community Foundation to
  administer the distribution of donated funds

RECOMMENDATION TO CITY COUNCIL

It is recommended that the City Council consider:

1.  Adopting a Resolution extending a local emergency resulting from the Mass
Murder on January 21, 2023 and authorizing the City Manager to execute an Executive
Order directing the California Community Foundation to administer the distribution of
donated funds; and

2.  Take such additional, related action that may be desirable.

CEQA (California Environmental Quality Act):

The Resolution itself and the actions anticipated by the Resolution were reviewed
pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (Public Resources Code §§ 21000,
et seq., “CEQA”) and the regulations promulgated thereunder (14 Cal. Code of
Regulations §§15000, et seq., the “CEQA Guidelines”). Based upon that review, this
action is exempt from further review pursuant to CEQA Guidelines § 15269(a) because
the protection of public and private property is necessary to maintain service essential to
the public, health and welfare.

BACKGROUND:

On January 21, 2023, the Monterey Park community was traumatized by the murder of
11 individuals and the injury of nine others. In the aftermath of that horrific incident, the
City’s resources are stretched thin. The Monterey Park Fire and Police Departments are
the most affected by addressing the public safety of the community; the other City
Departments, however, are also affected as we all are undergoing a “crash course” in
learning how to react to this tragedy. Under the circumstances, it is apparent that the local
emergency that was already in effect because of the 2023 Winter Storms must be
broadened to include the mobilization of public resources to meet the community’s needs
in healing from the January 21st incident.

In addition to a multitude of other matters, the outpouring of monetary donations must be
appropriately administered. While the City does have policies in place for accepting
donations (see, e.g., Resolution No. 11776 that is attached), the City simplyPagedoes

the expertise or capacity to undertake the important mission of ensuring that the funds so
generously contributed by persons around the world to support the victims’ families are
properly distributed. Accordingly, based upon the advice from other communities that
previously dealt with similar mass casualty incidents, the City Manager selected the
California Community Foundation (“CCF”) to partner with nonprofit corporations within the
community (that are already receiving donations) to act on the City’s behalf for the
purposes of coordinating the distribution of donated funds.

To implement this arrangement, it is crucial that the City issue an Executive Order. As
described in the draft Resolution, the Executive Order would make a final decision
regarding the arrangements with CCF; nomination persons for the contemplated
oversight board; authorize selection of the fund administrator; and, ultimately, the name
of the fund. The draft Resolution and Executive Order may be adopted or modified by the
City Council in its discretion.

It is crucial, however, that an Executive Order be issued by the City. Doing so will not only
allow the City to endorse the fund identified by the City Council, i.e., confirm its
trustworthiness and legitimacy, but will also ensure that those who receive monies from
that fund will not be further victimized by, for example, a tax burden that would be
otherwise imposed upon financial distributions from other sources. Also important is that
the City Council allow CCF and its other anticipated nonprofit partners – most notably the
Asian American Advancing Justice Southern California (“AAAJ So Cal”) – to form the
oversight board. This will help ensure that the partnership established between the City
and other nonprofits will share the responsibility of adopting and implementing protocols
for distributing donations.

FISCAL IMPACT:

Unknown at this time.

   RESOLUTION NO. ______

  A RESOLUTION ADOPTED BY THE CITY COUNCIL EXTENDING A LOCAL
  EMERGENCY RESULTING FROM THE MASS MURDER ON JANUARY 21,
  2023 AND RATIFYING THE CITY MANAGER’S ADMINISTRATIVE
  DECLARATION OF EMERGENCY AND EXECUTIVE ORDER DATED
  JANUARY 27, 2023.

  BE IT RESOLVED by the Council of the City of Monterey Park as follows:

SECTION 1: The City Council finds as follows:

  A.  On January 21, 2023, 11 people were murdered and nine were severely
  injured as the result of a shooting spree. This tragedy is unprecedented
  within the City’s history and will affect our community for many years in the
  future.

  B.  As a result of this tragic event, the City’s resources have been stretched
  thin: it was already addressing the local emergency declared earlier in
  January resulting from the 2023 Winter Storm systems and it is now
  addressing the aftermath of a violent and traumatic event that requires
  extensive resources.

  C.  The outpouring of support from federal, state, local and private sources
  has been overwhelmingly appreciated by the City Council and City
  administration. Additionally, persons all over the world have donated funds
  to assist with victims, their families, and other persons suffering as a result
  of the January 21st event.

  D.  The City does not currently have the resources to administer the collection
  and distribution of donations. Based upon the amounts already received, it
  is anticipated that significant time and effort will be needed to ensure that
  these funds are fairly and expeditiously distributed to those who need
  them.

  E.  Accordingly, the City anticipates partnering with several nonprofits
  including, without limitation, the Asian American Advancing Justice
  Southern California (“AAAJ So Cal”), to create the “Monterey Park Victim
  and Family Support Fund” or simply the “MPK Support Fund.” The MPK
  Support Fund is endorsed by the City of Monterey Park as the only official
  fund for accepting donations.

  F.  The MPK Support Fund will (a) provide a single vehicle to receive
  donations which immediately began pouring in from the public after
  January 21, 2023, and thereby avoid the misdirection of donations to
  fraudulent organizations; (2) provide the infrastructure to coordinate the

  Page 1 of 3

   collection, administration and distribution of these funds in a manner
  consistent with the City’s interest in assisting the victims of the attacks
  with financial and other restitution; (3) act as a central resource to allow
  those affected by the tragedy to find appropriate and reputable services;
  and (iv) maintain the infrastructure in coordination with the City Monterey
  Park that would allow it to respond immediately to city needs in the event
  of a similar tragedy, in order to lessen the burdens of government.

  G.  To help administer the distribution of donations through the MPK Support
  Fund, the City Council nominates the persons listed in the Executive
  Order signed by the City Manager on January 31, 2023, and such
  additional persons that may be identified by the City Council concurrently
  with adoption of this Resolution, to an oversight board comprised in the
  manner outlined in the Executive Order. Additionally, the City Council
  appoints a Fund Administrator who will be identified by the City Council
  concurrently with adoption of this Resolution or by the City Manager within
  two weeks after adoption of this Resolution with concurrence of the Mayor.

SECTION 2: Extension of Local Emergency. The City Council reviewed the state of
the community and extends the local emergency declared on January 8, 2023 (as
ratified by Resolution No. 2023-R5, adopted January 18, 2023) to include all actions
needed to react to the January 21, 2023 shooting incident. This Resolution supplements
Resolution No. 2023-R5 and confirms the ongoing local emergency

SECTION 3: Authorization of Executive Order. The City Council authorizes the City
Manager to execute the Executive Order attached as Exhibit “A,” which is incorporated
by reference, including the Emergency Policies and Procedures attached to that
Executive Order. The City Manager is authorized to modify the EP&P as may be
required to implement the intent and direction of this Resolution.

SECTION 4: Validity. If any part of this Resolution or its application is deemed invalid
by a court of competent jurisdiction, the City Council intends that such invalidity will not
affect the effectiveness of the remaining provisions or applications and, to this end, the
provisions of this Resolution are severable.

SECTION 5: Electronic Signatures. This Resolution may be executed with electronic
signatures in accordance with Government Code §16.5 and Monterey Park Municipal
Code Chapter 3.95. Such electronic signatures will be treated in all respects as having
the same effect as an original signature.

   CITY OF MONTEREY PARK

  EXECUTIVE ORDER
  JANUARY 31, 2023

The City of Monterey Park declares and orders as follows:

A local emergency exists within the City since January 8, 2023 in accordance with
the Administrative Declaration of Emergency as ratified by Resolution No. 2023-
R5, adopted January 18, 2023.

On January 21, 2023, the City experienced an unprecedented tragedy in the
murder of 11 individuals and the severe physical injury of nine others resulting from
a senseless shooting spree. This mass casualty incident (“MCI”) caused physical
injuries and trauma not only to the victims suffering gunshot wounds or other
physical injuries, but also to the witnesses to the crime Monterey Park community
as a whole.

Individuals, including residents of Monterey Park, residents of California, people
throughout the country and around the world, as well as numerous businesses,
exhibited extraordinary generosity in seeking to help those who were most
impacted by the MCI.

The City of Monterey Park recognizes the burdens imposed on it to field inquiries
for community support, collect gifts and monetary donations and ensure
appropriate distribution, assist the victims in receiving both financial and other
restitution, and provide a vehicle to centralize the community’s efforts to assist
those affected by the MCI.

In accordance with the Emergency Policies and Protocols (“EP&P”), attached as
Exhibit “A,” and incorporated by reference, the Monterey Park Victim and Family
Support Fund at the California Community Foundation (the “MPK Support Fund”),
was established concurrent with this Executive Order at the City’s request. Among
other things, the MPK Support Fund is intended to help distribute donations
received to help pay for emergency needs of impacted individuals and families who
lost loved ones.

The City of Monterey Park anticipates that all of the funds collected and pledged
to date will be distributed to those individuals and families most affected by the
MCI. Additionally, the City anticipates that the MPK Support Fund will receive a
continuing stream of contributions thereafter to continue to provide support for
those affected by the MCI.

To decrease the likelihood of people and organizations inadvertently donating
funds to fraudulent charities, it was deemed prudent to direct the California
  Page 1 of 2

  Page 9 of 28
 Community Foundation to operate the MPK Support Fund as the single vehicle
where donations could be channeled that would address the loss suffered by
victims and thereby lessen the governmental burdens. The MPK Support Fund will
be used to address these concerns.

The foregoing conditions constitute the existence of conditions presenting a
potential threat to the safety of persons and property within the City of Monterey
Park, which conditions are likely to be beyond the control of the services,
personnel, equipment and facilities of the City and require the combined forces of
other political subdivisions to combat.

Accordingly, I order that:

  1. The EP&P be implemented as written;

  2. The MPK Support Fund be the only official fund for accepting Donations
  the purpose of which is to reduce the governmental burdens generally
  caused by the MCI by alleviating the suffering of those directly harmed by
  that event; and

  3. That the local emergency declared January 8, 2023 be expanded to include
  all efforts needed to address the aftermath of the MCI described above and
  in the EP&P.

During the existence of said local emergency the powers, functions, and duties of
the emergency organization of the City of Monterey Park will be those prescribed
by state law, by ordinances, and resolutions of the City of Monterey Park.

  Ron Bow, City Manager

   EMERGENCY EXECUTIVE ORDER

  JANUARY 31, 2023

  MONTEREY PARK MASS CASUALTY INCIDENT

I.  Purpose

These emergency policies and procedures (“EP&P”) were adopted pursuant to Monterey Park
Municipal Code (“MPMC”) §§ 2.52.050 and 2.52.060; Resolution No. 2023-R5, adopted January
18, 2023; and Resolution No. 2023-RXX (adopted January 31, 2023) to protect public health,
safety, and welfare. These protocols are implemented to relieve the stress on City resources
including, without limitation, police officers; firefighters; public health professionals; public
works employees; and other public officials needed to address the aftermath of the January 21,
2023 mass casualty incident in which 11 people were murdered and nine individuals were
hospitalized (the “MCI”). The MCI caused both physical and mental injuries to hundreds of
individuals who witnessed the MCI; are families of the victims or witnesses; and are otherwise
affected by the traumatic circumstances of the MCI.

II.  Definitions

Unless the contrary is stated or clearly appears from the context, the following definitions govern
the construction of the words and phrases used in this EP&P. Words and phrases undefined in
this EP&P have the same meaning as set forth in applicable law.

  “Authorized Liaison” means those person(s) identified by the city of Monterey Park
  to organize and facilitate the creation of the Authorized Fund in order to lessen the
  City’s governmental burdens associated with the MCI.

  “Authorized Fund” means the “Monterey Park Victim and Family Support Fund,”
  or such other caption that may be established by the Oversight Committee,
  established with the California Community Foundation. The Authorized Fund is
  necessary to create a centralized vehicle for receiving and distributing the generous
  Donations; fielding inquiries for community support; assisting victims in receiving
  both financial and other restitution; and providing a vehicle to centralize the
  community’s efforts to assist those affected by the MCI.

  “Donations” means those monies deposited into the Authorized Fund for the
  purpose of assisting victims, victim families, and such other persons affected by the
  mass casualty incident on January 21, 2023.

  “Fund Administrator” means a person selected by the city of Monterey Park to
  implement the protocols adopted by the Oversight Board and distribute monies
  from the Authorized Fund.

  “Oversight Board” means a volunteer board comprised of community members
  selected by independent nonprofit corporations including, without limitation, the
  California Community Foundation (“CCF”), and nominated by the city of
  Monterey Park, responsible for adopting protocols to distribute monies from the
  Authorized Fund. Such protocols should govern the distribution of financial
  assistance to those most seriously affected by the MCI.

III.  Appointment of Authorized Liaison and Creation of Authorized Fund

By letter dated January 26, 2023, the California Community Foundation (“CCF”) is
appointed as the Authorized Liaison.

The City agrees to creation of the Authorized Fund. Unless its name is changed by the
Oversight Board, the Authorized Fund will be referred to as the “Monterey Park Victim
and Family Support Fund” or simply the “MPK Support Fund.” The MPK Support Fund
will be endorsed by the City of Monterey Park as the only official fund for accepting
Donations.

The Authorized Fund will (1) provide a single vehicle to receive Donations which
immediately began pouring in from the public in the wake of the MCI, and thereby avoid
the misdirection of donations to fraudulent organizations; (2) provide the infrastructure to
coordinate the collection, administration and distribution of these funds in a manner
consistent with the City’s interest in assisting the victims of the attacks with financial and
other restitution; (3) act as a central resource to allow those affected by the MCI to find
appropriate and reputable services; and (iv) maintain the infrastructure in coordination
with the City Monterey Park that would allow it to respond immediately to city needs in
the event of a similar tragedy, in order to lessen the burdens of government.

IV.  Oversight Board Nominees and Appointment of Fund Administrator

The City will appoint a Fund Administrator.

The City nominates City Treasurer Amy Lee; Ms. Anita Chu; Ms. Denise Jaramillo; Mr.
Hans Liang; Mr. Paul Talbot; Mr. Ricky Choi, Ms. Krystal Hamner and such additional
persons that may be identified by the City Council, for the Oversight Board. The
Authorized Fund and Authorized Liaison may appoint these, or other, persons as may be
desirable.

V.  Miscellaneous

Under no circumstance may the Donation of any individual or corporation having business
before the City or any agency thereof influence the decision of city officials in acting on such
business. Should any City officer or employee have reason to believe that such contribution is in
fact improperly influencing city officials, the reasons for such belief must be immediately
communicated to the City Manager or City Attorney, or any other appropriate investigatory
office, officer or body.

These EP&P are subject to review by the City Council in accordance with MPMC §
2.52.060(a)(6)(A). They will remain effective unless superseded by applicable federal or state
law; or are terminated by the City Council or City Manager.

   RESOLUTION NO. 11776

  A RESOLUTION ESTABLISHING POLICIES AND PROCEDURES FOR
  ACCEPTING CONTRIBUTIONS, DONATIONS, GIFTS, BEQUESTS, AND
  DEVISES FOR PUBLIC PURPOSES.

  The City Council of the City of Monterey Park does hereby resolve as follows

SECTION 1: The City Council finds and declares as follows

  A  Community members seeking to improve the City's services, contribute to
  the construction of important public facilities, or othenruise seeking to
  enhance the City frequently seek to make contributions, donations, gifts,
  bequests, or devises (collectively, "donations") to the City;

  B  A review of the City's documents show that there are no existing policies
  for accepting such generous donations;

  c  It is in the public interest for the City to establish policies for accepting
  donations so that persons making such donations may take appropriate
  tax deductions, the City uses donations for the purpose for which they
  were intended, and so the City's administration has clear direction
  regarding what kinds of donations should be accepted;

  D  The City Council, or its designee, may accept or reject any donation for
  any public purpose. In doing so, the City may keep or dispose such
  donations or use them in the manner required by the donor;

  E  Unless otherwise specified by the donor, the City may use donations in
  any manner it chooses to promote the public interest;

  F  Contributions to the City may be tax deductible as a charitable contribution
  if the donation is made exclusively for a public purpose (26 U.S.C. S
  170(cX1)). For example, without limitation, art education is a legitimate
  public purpose (Government Code S 15813).

SECTION 2: Definitions. Unless the contrary is stated or clearly appears from the
context, the following definitions will govern the construction of the words and phrases
used in this chapter.

  A.  "City manager" means the city manager or designee;

  B.  "Donation" means a contribution, donation, gift, bequest or devise of
  personal or real property, but not personal services. Donations may be
  solicited or unsolicited by the City;

FROM:  Matthew Hallock, Fire Chief
SUBJECT:  Fiscal Year 2022 Assistance to Firefighters Grants (AFG) Program

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  1. Approving the Fiscal Year 2022 Assistance to Firefighters Grant (AFG) Program
  for consideration of AFG funding;
  2. Authorizing the City’s Finance Department to allocate $8,416.12 from the City
  Budget to fund the required applicant match if the grant is awarded;
  3. Adopting a resolution authorizing the City Manager or designee, to apply for,
  receive, and appropriate grant funds for the Fiscal Year 2022 Assistance to
  Firefighters Grant Program; and
  4. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
The City of Monterey Park Fire Department received Notice of Funding Opportunity
(NOFO) from Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) regarding a formal
invitation to submit a full application for consideration of AFG funds. If the City is
offered a grant award, the total proposed budget request is $92,577.35, which includes
a federal share request of $84,161.23 and a required applicant match of $8,416.12. The
application Activity Title is Personal Protective Equipment: Air Compressor/Fill
Station/Cascade System Replacement.

Staff seeks City Council consideration and approval of the City of Monterey Park’s
AFG application. The application due date is February 10, 2023. When the grant
award decision is made and if the grant award is received, staff will inform City
Council.

BACKGROUND:
The Assistance to Firefighters Grants (AFG) was established under FEMA in 2001 as
a funding resource for firefighters and first responders to obtain the necessary tools,
equipment, and other critical resources needed to safely perform job duties while
protecting the public.

  Page 18 of 28

January 31, 2023

The Fire Department (Department) seeks funding to update the air compressor
system (system) in Fire Station 61. The system is used by the firefighters to fill their
self-contained breathing apparatuses (SCBAs) with oxygen. The SCBAs are used to
supply oxygen to firefighters responding to fire related incidents; and are considered
critical Personal Protective Equipment (PPE).

The SCBAs will expire in the forthcoming years. The current air compressor will be
inoperable with the new equipment. The system is over 20 years old and cannot be
retrofitted to comply with new industry standards. In anticipation of new SCBAs, staff
seeks to replace the legacy system with an upgraded air compressor system.

If the City of Monterey Park is offered a grant award, the total proposed budget
request is $92,577.35, which includes a federal share request of $84,161.23 and a
required applicant match of $8,416.12. Per AFG, the required applicant match is
factored in accordance with the size of the applicant’s jurisdiction. For jurisdictions with
a population of 20,000 but less than 1,000,000, a ten percent match is required.

Staff seeks City Council consideration and approval of the City of Monterey Park’s
AFG application, which also includes the authorization of funding the required applicant
match. The due date to submit the application and required documents is February 10,
2023. The application period of performance will not exceed 24 months. If the grant
award is offered, the City of Monterey Park will complete the update before the
timeframe. When the grant award decision is made and if the grant award is received,
staff will inform City Council.

FISCAL IMPACT:
Potential impact to the City’s adopted fiscal year budget would be contingent upon
whether the application is approved and if the grant award is received. If the City is
offered a grant award, the total proposed budget request is $92,577.35, which includes
a Federal Share Request of $84,161.23 and a Required Applicant Match of $8,416.12.
A budget appropriation of $8,416.12 from the General Fund is requested for the
required application match.

  MINUTES
  MONTEREY PARK CITY COUNCIL
  FINANCING AUTHORITY (MPFA)

  SUCCESSOR AGENCY (SA)
  SPECIAL MEETING
  JANUARY 31, 2023

The City Council, the Financing Authority (MPFA), the Housing Authority (MPHA), the
Geologic Hazard Abatement District (GHAD), and the Successor Agency (SA) of the City
of Monterey Park held a Special Meeting of the Council in the Council Chamber, located
at 320 West Newmark Avenue in the City of Monterey Park, Tuesday, January 31, 2023
at 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER:
Mayor Sanchez called the meeting to order at 6:06 p.m.

FLAG SALUTE:
Mayor Sanchez conducted the flag salute.

ROLL CALL:
City Clerk Maychelle Yee called the roll:

Council Members Present:  Henry Lo, Vinh Ngo, Jose Sanchez, Thomas Wong
Council Members Absent:  Yvonne Liu

ALSO PRESENT: City Attorney Karl Berger, City Manager Ron Bow, City Treasurer Amy
Lee, Assistant City Manager Inez Alvarez, Police Chief Scott Wiese, Battalion Chief Ryan
Weddle, City Librarian Diana Garcia, Director of Finance Martha Garcia, Director of
Human Resources Christine Tomikawa, Interim Planning Director Jessica Serrano,
Deputy City Clerk Cindy Trang

VIRTUALLY PRESENT: Director of Public Works Shawn Igoe, Director of Recreation &
Community Services Robert Aguirre, Carol Bradford Worley (representative for California
Community Foundation)

AGENDA ADDITIONS, DELETIONS, CHANGES AND ADOPTIONS
None

PUBLIC COMMUNICATIONS

  - Maychelle Yee, resident and City Clerk, voiced a concern from a constituent
  regarding the city’s fire personnel not getting enough recognition for their heroic
  effort on the night of the mass shooting. She took a moment to thank the

  MISSION STATEMENT
  The mission of the City of Monterey Park is to provide excellent services to enhance
  the quality of life for our entire community
   71-16
  January 31, 2023
  firefighters for their composure, resilience, and professionalism during this tragic
  event. She also reminded everyone that counseling services are available at the
  library.

1.  NEW BUSINESS

1A.  ADOPT A RESOLUTION EXTENDING A LOCAL EMERGENCY RESULTING
  FROM THE MASS MURDER ON JANUARY 21, 2023 AND AUTHORIZING THE
  CITY MANAGER TO ISSUE AN EXECUTIVE ORDER TO DIRECT THE
  CALIFORNIA COMMUNITY FOUNDATION TO ADMINISTER THE
  DISTRIBUTION OF DONATED FUNDS

  On January 21, 2023, the Monterey Park community was traumatized by the
  murder of 11 individuals and the injury of nine others. In the aftermath of that
  horrific incident, the City’s resources are stretched thin. The Monterey Park Fire
  and Police Departments are the most affected by addressing the public safety of
  the community; the other City Departments, however, are also affected as we all
  are undergoing a “crash course” in learning how to react to this tragedy. Under the
  circumstances, it is apparent that the local emergency that was already in effect
  because of the 2023 Winter Storms must be broadened to include the mobilization
  of public resources to meet the community’s needs in healing from the January
  21st incident.

  CEQA (California Environmental Quality Act)
  The Resolution itself and the actions anticipated by the Resolution were reviewed
  pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (Public Resources Code §§
  21000, et seq., “CEQA”) and the regulations promulgated thereunder (14 Cal.
  Code of Regulations §§15000, et seq., the “CEQA Guidelines”). Based upon that
  review, this action is exempt from further review pursuant to CEQA Guidelines §
  15269(a) because the protection of public and private property is necessary to
  maintain service essential to the public, health and welfare.

  SUPPLEMENTAL – LOCAL EMERGENCY RESULTING FROM MASS
  CASUALTY INCIDENT ON JANUARY 21, 2023

  A supplemental staff report for Item 1-A. Based upon conversations with
  representatives at the County of Los Angeles Office of Emergency Management
  (“OEM”) on January 31, 2023, it is recommended that the City Council declare a
  new local emergency resulting from the Mass Casualty Incident on January 21,
  2023. This is in lieu of extending the local emergency already in effect for the
  Winter Storms of 2023. Changes reflecting this recommendation were made to the
  draft resolution and executive order; they accompany to the Supplemental Staff
  Report in redline format for easy reference.
   71-17
  January 31, 2023
  Discussion: The Supplemental Staff Report was presented to the City Council
  and made available to the public. Carol Bradford Worley, Chief Legal Officer of
  California Community Foundation (CCF), provided general information on the role
  of the Foundation and how funds will be received and distributed. City Attorney
  Berger stated that the Emergency Policies and Protocols (EP&P) can be changed
  administratively to add additional Oversight Board members.

  Recommendation: (1) Adopting a Resolution extending a local emergency
  resulting from the Mass Murder on January 21, 2023 and authorizing the City
  Manager to execute an Executive Order directing the California Community
  Foundation to administer the distribution of donated funds; and (2) Take such
  additional, related action that may be desirable.

  Action Taken: The City Council adopted Resolution No. 2023-R7 declaring a new
  local emergency regarding the Mass Murder on January 21, 2023 and authorized
  the City Manager to execute an Executive Order directing the California
  Community Foundation to administer the distribution of donated funds as
  presented in the Supplemental Staff Report as amended to include the City
  Manager with concurrence of the Mayor as Fund Administrators and
  recommended the following individuals to the oversight board: Judge Bryant Yang,
  Judge Ed Chau, Rick Eng, and Gay Yuen, but ultimately leaving the decision to
  California Community Foundation to seat the Oversight Board.

  Motion: Moved by Mayor Pro Tem Wong and seconded by Mayor Sanchez motion
  carried by the following vote:

  Ayes:  Council Members:  Lo, Ngo, Wong, Sanchez
  Noes:  Council Members:  None
  Absent:  Council Members:  Yiu
  Abstain:  Council Members:  None

  Resolution No. 2023-R7:
  A RESOLUTION ADOPTED BY THE CITY COUNCIL DECLARING A LOCAL
  EMERGENCY RESULTING FROM THE MASS MURDER ON JANUARY 21, 2023
  AND AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO EXECUTE AN EXECUTIVE
  ORDER DATED JANUARY 31, 2023

1B.  FISCAL YEAR 2022 ASSISTANCE TO FIREFIGHTERS GRANTS (AFG)
  PROGRAM

  The City of Monterey Park Fire Department received Notice of Funding Opportunity
  (NOFO) from Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) regarding a
  formal invitation to submit a full application for consideration of AFG funds. If the
  City is offered a grant award, the total proposed budget request is $92,577.35,
  which includes a federal share request of $84,161.23 and a required applicant
   71-18
  January 31, 2023
  match of $8,416.12. The application Activity Title is Personal Protective
  Equipment: Air Compressor/Fill Station/Cascade System Replacement.

  Staff seeks City Council consideration and approval of the City of Monterey Park’s
  AFG application. The application due date is February 10, 2023. When the grant
  award decision is made and if the grant award is received, staff will inform City
  Council.

  Action Taken: The City Council (1) approved the Fiscal Year 2022 Assistance to
  Firefighters Grant (AFG) Program for consideration of AFG funding; (2) authorized
  the City’s Finance Department to allocate $8,416.12 from the City Budget to fund
  the required applicant match if the grant is awarded; (3) adopted Resolution No.
  2023-R8 authorizing the City Manager or designee, to apply for, receive, and
  appropriate grant funds for the Fiscal Year 2022 Assistance to Firefighters Grant
  Program.

  Motion: Moved by Council Member Lo and seconded by Council Member Ngo,
  motion carried by the following vote:

  Ayes:  Council Members:  Lo, Ngo, Wong, Sanchez
  Noes:  Council Members:  None
  Absent:  Council Members:  Yiu
  Abstain:  Council Members:  None

  Resolution No. 2023-R8:
  A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER, OR DESIGNEE, TO
  APPLY FOR, RECEIVE, AND APPROPRIATE GRANT FUNDS FOR THE FISCAL
  YEAR 2022 ASSISTANCE TO FIREFIGHTERS GRANTS PROGRAM –
  PERSONAL  PROTECTIVE  EQUIPMENT:  AIR  COMPRESSOR/FILL
  STATION/CASCADE SYSTEM REPLACEMENT

CITY COMMUNICATIONS (CITY COUNCIL)

  Council Member Lo noted that he went to the Lunar New Year celebration in the
  City of Alhambra, where Brandon Tsay was honored for his heroic action on
  January 21, 2023. He also mentioned, while Mayor at the time, he contacted
  Deborah Penrose, Mayor of Halfmoon Bay City, to offer condolences on their city’s
  recent tragedy and to offer assistance, if needed. He spoke on gun violence and
  how it should be on a future agenda, in addition to how the community should
  recover.

  Council Member Ngo spoke about the recent suffering the City and the community
  has experienced over the past ten days as we grieve, heal and move on. He
  reported that he attended the Lunar New Year Festival in Alhambra and the Golden
  Dragon Parade in Chinatown, Los Angeles. He expressed his gratitude to the city
  personnel and first responders for their help.
   71-19
  January 31, 2023

  Mayor Pro Tem Wong voiced his solidarity with the community in mourning the
  tragedy that took place and will continue to foster a sense of community by offering
  the resources and services it requires. He stressed the need of assisting
  neighborhood organizations and local businesses to demonstrate that it is safe to
  venture outside. In addition, he wanted to reiterate what Council Member Ngo said
  and that this act of hatred will not define us, and that resources are available to
  meet the community’s needs. He said that it is very encouraging to see the support
  of the community and for everyone to come together through this healing process.
  He also asked Karl about the new law of SB 1439.

  Mayor Sanchez mentioned that Brandon Tsay will be honored by Monterey Park
  at the upcoming City Council meeting and urges everyone to attend and show their
  support. He also thanked the local businesses, congregations, and towns that have
  organized vigils over the past ten days. He said that he frequently attends these
  vigils and that he would be open to any additional invitations from other
  organizations. He expressed his happiness that local cities were still celebrating
  Lunar New Year. According to him, it is crucial to continue the celebration in order
  to honor our community’s diversity and culture as well as to maintain normalcy. He
  thanked city staff and first responders for all their efforts. He also commended
  Council Member Lo for serving as the Mayor during this tragedy and echoed the
  same sentiments regarding the essential improvements in this nation’s gun laws.

ADJOURNMENT
There being no further business for consideration, the meeting was adjourned at 7:21
p.m.
